example_5_1.name: Example 5.1 (L^2-bounded)
example_5_1.analytical_notes: Example 5.1: H_1 = {a_n * xi_n} with xi_n ~ N(0,1) i.i.d., a_n in [0.5, 2.0], truncated to K=50. Bounded in L^0 via sup P(|h|>=t) <= a_dagger^2/t^2 -> 0 (Chebyshev). Closure in L^0: each individual variable is L^2, and the closure of the convex hull is compact in L^2 and hence in L^0 by inclusion. Zero excluded: a_n >= a_star > 0 and xi_n are nondegenerate.

example_5_2.name: Example 5.2 (Cauchy, L^0-bounded only)
example_5_2.analytical_notes: Example 5.2: H_2 = {c_n * zeta_n} with zeta_n ~ Cauchy(0,1) i.i.d., c_n in [0.5, 2.0], truncated to K=50. Bounded in L^0 via sup P(|h|>=t) <= 2/pi * arctan(c_dag/t) -> 0 as t->inf. KEY INSIGHT: L^0-boundedness holds despite E[|zeta_n|] = infinity. This example validates that small-cone structure is weaker than L^1/L^2 boundedness and hence applies to heavy-tailed payoff families. Zero excluded: c_n >= c_star > 0 and Cauchy r.v.s are nondegenerate.

example_5_3.name: Example 5.3 (Finite-dim)
example_5_3.analytical_notes: Example 5.3: H_3 = finite family of 4 linearly independent generators on S=10 states (uniform p). SC1: conv(H_3) is a polytope (closed and convex). SC2: Finite family => trivially closed in L^0. SC3: Bounded in L^0 since max |g_k| < inf on finite omega. SC4: All generators nonzero = True. Zero in conv(H_3) = False. (For SC4 we need 0 not in H_3, which holds since generators are nonzero.)

nonredundancy.note: K_0 ∩ (-L) = {0} — small cone is nonredundant w.r.t. dynamic trading.

closedness.justification: In a finite-state (finite-dimensional) setting, any finitely-generated cone C + L is closed in R^S (which is L^0 of the finite probability space). This directly illustrates Lemma 2.4's conclusion under the assumption that C ∩ (-L) = {0}.
